OBJECT_MODEL.note: Conceptual only. No DDL, no column types beyond what is needed to make an invariant checkable, no migration ordinal. Names below are the CONCEPTUAL names an implementing node must carry; they preserve RE_U3's target_model vocabulary.

objects.purpose: Organization-scoped named container for a family of template versions. Holds only mutable identity metadata (name, description, archived_at) — never criteria and never DecisionPolicy.
objects.cross_org_prohibition: A template is NEVER shared across organizations and NEVER platform-global. There is no system template, no seeded global template and no template library outside an organization (CS-11).

objects.scope: ORGANIZATION (denormalized organization_id, so RLS never needs a join to be correct)
objects.purpose: The IMMUTABLE unit. Carries the criteria/dimension structure AND the DecisionPolicy for that version. This is the object EV-02 means by 'immutable/versioned template policy'.
objects.mutability: APPEND-ONLY. Once a row exists it is never updated. Publication is expressed by a separate immutable transition record or by an immutable published_at written in the same statement that creates the row — never by a later UPDATE.

objects.re_u3_model_node: Evaluation + deterministic Score + Recommendation + Human Decision
objects.scope: ORGANIZATION, bound to exactly one project
objects.purpose: One evaluation instance: a project assessed against one immutable template version. Carries the state machine and, at DECIDED, the immutable decision snapshot.
objects.mutability: Workflow columns are mutable ONLY while state is pre-DECIDED. Every snapshot column is write-once and immutable from the moment state becomes DECIDED.
required_columns_conceptual: template_version_id NOT NULL — pinned at creation, never repointed
state NOT NULL with a CLOSED CHECK over the five STATE_MACHINE states
designated_decision_role NOT NULL with a CLOSED CHECK over exactly ('organization_admin','impact_manager'), default 'organization_admin'
score_snapshot NULLABLE numeric, write-once at DECIDED
score_status_snapshot NULLABLE with a CLOSED CHECK over ('COMPUTED','SCORE_NOT_COMPUTABLE'), write-once at DECIDED
recommendation_snapshot NULLABLE with a CLOSED CHECK over the three DECISION_OUTCOMES, write-once at DECIDED
decision_policy_hash_snapshot NULLABLE, write-once at DECIDED, copied from OBJ-2.decision_policy_hash
decision_outcome NULLABLE with a CLOSED CHECK over the three DECISION_OUTCOMES, write-once at DECIDED
decision_rationale NULLABLE text, write-once at DECIDED
decided_by_role NULLABLE with a CLOSED CHECK over exactly ('organization_admin','impact_manager'), write-once at DECIDED
objects.no_stored_divergence_column: There is deliberately NO divergence column. Divergence is DERIVED. See DIVERGENCE_CONTROLS.DIV-02.
objects.no_stella_columns: There is deliberately NO stella_recommendation, stella_score, stella_outcome or stella_analysis column on this object. See STELLA_BOUNDARY.SB-04.

objects.scope: ORGANIZATION, bound to exactly one evaluation
objects.purpose: The per-criterion human INPUT. Carries the governed-N/A state, its mandatory rationale and its human provenance (EV-01).
objects.mutability: Upsertable while the parent evaluation is pre-DECIDED; frozen once the parent is DECIDED.
required_columns_conceptual: criterion_key NOT NULL — must resolve against the pinned template_version_id's criteria_json
response_kind NOT NULL with a CLOSED CHECK over ('SCORED','NOT_APPLICABLE')
score_value NULLABLE — NOT NULL when response_kind = 'SCORED', and NULL when response_kind = 'NOT_APPLICABLE'
na_rationale NULLABLE — NOT NULL and non-empty when response_kind = 'NOT_APPLICABLE' (EV-01 requires explicit state, rationale AND human provenance)
objects.governed_na_contract: response_kind = 'NOT_APPLICABLE' requires na_rationale to be present and non-empty AND recorded_by to be a real user. A NULL score with no explicit NOT_APPLICABLE state is NOT a governed N/A — it is an UNANSWERED criterion, which is a different thing and blocks READY_FOR_DECISION rather than being excluded from the denominator.

explicitly_not_created.reason: CS-16. The Score and the Recommendation are DERIVED from OBJ-4 plus the pinned OBJ-2 at read time, and SNAPSHOTTED onto OBJ-3 at DECIDED. A separate results relation would create a second source of truth that could drift from the inputs that produced it.
CS-17. These are FIBDB-019 and FIBDB-020, owned by FIBIU-20 (wave 3, topological_level 3.2). Evaluate must not annex another FIBIU's objects and must not gate itself on them.
CS-09 says divergence is DERIVED. A stored divergence row could disagree with the two snapshots it claims to summarize.

EV-02 places DecisionPolicy INSIDE the immutable versioned template policy. A standalone relation would create a second version lineage that could be repointed independently of the template version an evaluation pinned.

explicitly_not_created.object: any Evaluate report / locator / verification-hash object

DECIDED_REUSE_REFUSALS.candidate: domain_object_versions as the Evaluate snapshot/version substrate
DECIDED_REUSE_REFUSALS.why_it_looked_free: It is append-only, guarded by uellix_forbid_mutation, has (object_type, object_id, ordinal) UNIQUE and a payload_json + content_hash pair, and its object_type is varchar(100) with NO CHECK — so a new 'evaluation_template_version' object_type would need no DDL at all.
DECIDED_REUSE_REFUSALS.refused_because: db/migrations/0045 defines domain_object_versions_select as USING (organization_id = ANY(current_user_org_ids()) OR current_user_is_super_admin()). Storing Evaluate template criteria, DecisionPolicy or decision content there would place that content behind a STANDING platform-superadmin read bypass, which CS-12 forbids and MO-07 requires an explicit exclusion for. The apparently free reuse is exactly the one that breaks the invariant.
DECIDED_REUSE_REFUSALS.disposition: REFUSED. Evaluate carries its own relations with bypass-free policies. domain_object_versions may still be used for Evaluate objects that carry NO evaluation content, but this package authorizes no such use.

DECIDED_REUSE_REFUSALS.candidate: governed_model_registry as the DecisionPolicy version identity
DECIDED_REUSE_REFUSALS.why_it_looked_free: It is exactly a version-identity relation: (model_id, version) UNIQUE plus definition_hash, already the precedent for rubric_version as a value-reference.
DECIDED_REUSE_REFUSALS.refused_because: It has NO organization_id column. It is a GLOBAL relation. Organization-scoped templates (CS-11) cannot have their policy identity live in a global registry without either leaking template identity across organizations or smuggling organization_id into model_id as a string.
DECIDED_REUSE_REFUSALS.disposition: REFUSED as the storage location. ADOPTED as the PATTERN: (owner, version) UNIQUE plus a content hash, applied inside OBJ-2 with organization_id present.

DECIDED_REUSE_REFUSALS.refused_because: readiness_score is a MANUAL human INPUT, not a computed score. Reusing it would make SCORE and INPUT the same object, violating RE_U3's ratified INPUT != SCORE separation.
It carries UNIQUE (project, step) — one row per pipeline step per project. Evaluate criteria are per (evaluation, criterion) against a pinned template version, a different cardinality entirely.

DECIDED_REUSE_REFUSALS.candidate: a new stella_role value for Evaluate on stella_interactions
DECIDED_REUSE_REFUSALS.refused_because: stella_interactions_stella_role_check is a CLOSED CHECK over exactly six values. Adding one is DDL, and it is DDL on a table this package has no authority to alter.
DECIDED_REUSE_REFUSALS.disposition: DEFERRED, not refused. See STELLA_BOUNDARY.SB-05 and DDL_FUTURE.

states.meaning: Created and bound to a template version; no criterion responses required yet.
At least one criterion response recorded; responses are upsertable.

Every criterion of the pinned template version has a response (SCORED or governed NOT_APPLICABLE). The Score and the SYSTEM Recommendation are computable and displayed, but nothing is snapshotted yet.
A designated human recorded an outcome. All snapshot columns are written in the SAME statement and are immutable thereafter.
Withdrawn before any decision was recorded. Reachable ONLY from a pre-DECIDED state (CS-10).

STATE_MACHINE.score_status_is_not_a_state: SCORE_NOT_COMPUTABLE is deliberately NOT a state. It is a DERIVED property of the current criterion responses against the pinned template version, recomputed on every read. Making it a state would let a stored value go stale relative to the responses that determine it, and a stale 'COMPUTED' would unblock a decision that must be blocked. It is enforced as a GUARD on the DECIDED transition (T5) instead.
STATE_MACHINE.archived_is_terminal_and_pre_decision_on: There is NO transition out of ARCHIVED and NO transition from DECIDED to ARCHIVED. An organization that wants to withdraw a decided evaluation must record that as a NEW evaluation, because a decided evaluation is audit-bearing evidence that a human decided (CS-10).

guards: template_version_id resolves to a PUBLISHED OBJ-2 row in the SAME organization
project_id resolves in the SAME organization
designated_decision_role defaults to 'organization_admin' and, if supplied, is a member of EVALUATE_DECISION_ROLES
criterion_key resolves against the PINNED template version
governed-N/A contract satisfied when response_kind = NOT_APPLICABLE
EVERY criterion of the pinned template version has a response — no UNANSWERED criterion remains
actor's role in THIS organization equals the evaluation's designated_decision_role
actor's role is a member of EVALUATE_DECISION_ROLES (belt and braces against a designated_decision_role somehow written outside the closed set)
score_status computed NOW equals 'COMPUTED' — a 'SCORE_NOT_COMPUTABLE' status REFUSES the transition (CS-03)
decision_outcome is a member of DECISION_OUTCOMES
when decision_outcome != recommendation_snapshot, decision_rationale is present and non-empty (CS-09)
all snapshot columns written in the SAME statement as the state change

forbidden_transitions.reason: DECIDED is terminal; snapshots are immutable.
ARCHIVED is terminal and pre-decision; a withdrawn evaluation can never acquire a decision.
A decision requires a complete response set; T3 cannot be skipped.
A decision requires a complete response set; T3 cannot be skipped.

TRANSITION_MATRIX.enforcement_layers: The transition matrix is enforced in the SERVER ACTION (authoritative) and, where a transition is also expressible as a database constraint, additionally at the database as defense in depth. A UI that hides a button is NOT an enforcement layer.

SCORING.determinism: The Score is a PURE function of (the pinned template version's criteria_json, the complete set of OBJ-4 responses). It reads no clock, no random source, no environment variable and no AI output. The same inputs always yield the same Score.
SCORING.governed_na_arithmetic: Per EV-01, a criterion whose response_kind = 'NOT_APPLICABLE' is excluded from the numerator AND the denominator. It is not scored as zero and it is not scored as the maximum.
SCORING.readiness_is_a_different_domain: EV-01 explicitly permits Measure readiness to use a different governed-N/A arithmetic. This package binds ONLY Evaluate scoring. It does NOT change, reinterpret or align lib/pipeline readiness arithmetic, and an implementer must not refactor the two into a shared helper on the assumption that they agree.

score_status.COMPUTED: The denominator is greater than zero — at least one criterion is SCORED.
score_status.SCORE_NOT_COMPUTABLE: The denominator is ZERO. Every criterion of the pinned template version resolved to governed NOT_APPLICABLE, so EV-01's exclusion rule removes every term from both numerator and denominator.
score_status.derivation: score_status is computed, never stored outside the DECIDED snapshot.

SCORING.unanswered_is_not_na: An UNANSWERED criterion (no OBJ-4 row at all) is NOT a governed N/A. It blocks T3 rather than being excluded from the denominator. Conflating the two would let an empty evaluation reach READY_FOR_DECISION with a vacuous SCORE_NOT_COMPUTABLE and would make CS-03's block indistinguishable from ordinary incompleteness.

ZERO_DENOMINATOR_CONTROLS.control: SCORE_NOT_COMPUTABLE is the NAME of the zero-denominator condition, not a separate error path.
ZERO_DENOMINATOR_CONTROLS.rationale: EV-01's rule — N/A excluded from numerator AND denominator — makes an all-N/A evaluation arithmetically scoreless BY CONSTRUCTION. CS-03's 'SCORE_NOT_COMPUTABLE blocks decision' and the zero-denominator control the coordinator asked for are therefore THE SAME MECHANISM, not two. An implementation with a separate divide-by-zero guard and a separate SCORE_NOT_COMPUTABLE flag has two things that can disagree.

ZERO_DENOMINATOR_CONTROLS.control: The scoring function NEVER performs a division whose denominator it has not first proven greater than zero. It returns a discriminated result carrying score_status, not a number plus a nullable error.

No NaN, no Infinity, no null-coerced-to-zero and no sentinel numeric value (such as -1 or 0) may ever represent SCORE_NOT_COMPUTABLE. A sentinel number would be comparable against DecisionPolicy thresholds and could silently produce a recommendation.

The SYSTEM Recommendation is NOT produced when score_status = 'SCORE_NOT_COMPUTABLE'. The recommendation is absent, not defaulted to 'reject' and not defaulted to 'approve_with_conditions'. A default would be the system deciding.
T5 REFUSES when score_status computed at decision time is 'SCORE_NOT_COMPUTABLE'. The refusal is server-authoritative and audited as a refusal, never a silent no-op.

A template version whose criteria_json contains ZERO criteria may not be published. An empty criteria set makes every evaluation against it permanently SCORE_NOT_COMPUTABLE, which is a template defect, not a governed outcome.

DECISION_OUTCOMES.note: Exactly these three, exactly these spellings (CS-04). Enforced as a CLOSED CHECK constraint on OBJ-3.decision_outcome AND on OBJ-3.recommendation_snapshot, and as a closed union in the type layer. No 'pending', no 'deferred', no 'abstain', no null-as-outcome. An evaluation with no outcome is expressed by its STATE, not by a fourth outcome value.
DECISION_OUTCOMES.shared_domain_is_deliberate: recommendation_snapshot and decision_outcome draw from the SAME closed set of three. That is what makes divergence computable as a simple inequality (DIV-02). If the SYSTEM recommendation had its own vocabulary, divergence would require a mapping table and the mapping would become a place to hide a disagreement.

DECISION_POLICY.definition: The DecisionPolicy is the deterministic function that maps a COMPUTED Score to exactly one member of DECISION_OUTCOMES. It is data, stored as decision_policy_json inside the immutable OBJ-2 row (EV-02: 'DecisionPolicy belongs to an immutable/versioned template policy').
determinism_requirements: Total over the score domain: for every possible COMPUTED score value the policy yields exactly one outcome. No gap, no overlap.
Band boundaries are explicit and closed on a stated side. A policy that leaves a boundary value ambiguous is not publishable.
The policy reads ONLY the Score. It does not read the actor, the project, the clock, the organization's plan, or any Stella output.
No fallback branch. A policy needing a fallback is not total and must be rejected at publication, not patched at evaluation time.

version_identity.identity_is: The DecisionPolicy version identity IS the template version identity. There is no second, independent policy version lineage.
components: definition_hash (over the whole immutable version payload)
version_identity.why_two_hashes: definition_hash proves the whole version is unchanged. decision_policy_hash proves specifically WHICH policy produced a recommendation, so a snapshotted recommendation stays attributable even if a future authority ever permits any other part of a version to be amended. OBJ-3 snapshots decision_policy_hash_snapshot, not the policy body.
version_identity.pattern_source: governed_model_registry's (model_id, version) UNIQUE plus definition_hash, adopted as a PATTERN and re-hosted inside an organization-scoped relation (see DRR-02).
version_identity.immutability_enforcement: UPDATE and DELETE denied by RLS policy OMISSION on OBJ-2, plus the uellix_forbid_mutation trigger as defense in depth — the 0045 precedent verbatim, including its stated position that the trigger is 'defense in depth, not the only guard'.

DECISION_POLICY.pinning: An evaluation pins template_version_id at creation (T1) and that pin is NEVER repointed. Publishing a new template version has ZERO effect on any existing evaluation, decided or not. A recommendation is therefore always reproducible from the version that produced it.

SYSTEM_RECOMMENDATION.producer: The SYSTEM, deterministically, from (Score, pinned immutable DecisionPolicy). Never Stella, never a human, never a default (CS-01, EV-02).
SYSTEM_RECOMMENDATION.visibility: Displayed in the in-app read model whenever score_status = 'COMPUTED', from READY_FOR_DECISION onward. It is ADVICE TO THE HUMAN, and it never auto-applies.
SYSTEM_RECOMMENDATION.snapshot: At T5, recommendation_snapshot is written in the SAME statement as decision_outcome. It records what the system recommended AT THE MOMENT OF DECISION.
SYSTEM_RECOMMENDATION.why_snapshot_rather_than_recompute: CS-09 requires divergence to be derived from the SNAPSHOTTED recommendation. Recomputing the recommendation later — from a template version that could in principle be superseded, or from responses that a future authority might permit amending — would make a historical divergence finding change after the fact. A snapshot makes the divergence record permanent.
SYSTEM_RECOMMENDATION.no_auto_decision: There is no path, flag, cron, batch job or admin action by which the SYSTEM recommendation becomes the decision without a designated human performing T5. 'Human decision remains decisive' (EV-02) is enforced by the absence of any such path, and NSB-05 is the control that proves the absence.

DIVERGENCE_CONTROLS.control: Divergence exists only for a DECIDED evaluation. A pre-DECIDED evaluation has no decision_outcome, so it has no divergence VALUE at all — which is different from having a divergence of 'false'.
Divergence is DERIVED as (recommendation_snapshot IS NOT NULL AND decision_outcome != recommendation_snapshot). It is computed from the two snapshot columns on read. It is NOT stored (CS-09).
DIVERGENCE_CONTROLS.rationale: A stored divergence flag is a third value that can disagree with the two it summarizes. Deriving it makes disagreement impossible by construction.

DIVERGENCE_CONTROLS.control: decision_rationale is MANDATORY when decision_outcome != recommendation_snapshot, enforced server-side at T5 AND as a database CHECK constraint over the row (a decided row where the two outcomes differ and decision_rationale is NULL or empty must be unrepresentable, not merely unreachable through the action).
DIVERGENCE_CONTROLS.rationale: CS-09. Enforcing this only in the action leaves the invariant true by convention rather than by construction.

DIVERGENCE_CONTROLS.control: decision_rationale is PERMITTED but not required when decision_outcome == recommendation_snapshot. Agreement needs no justification; disagreement does.

A decided evaluation whose score_status_snapshot is 'SCORE_NOT_COMPUTABLE' cannot exist, because T5 refuses that case (ZD-05). Therefore recommendation_snapshot is NEVER NULL on a DECIDED row, and divergence is always well-defined for a decided evaluation. Stated explicitly so no implementer adds a 'divergence unknown' third value to cover a case the state machine already forecloses.

Divergence is auditable WITHOUT reading rationale text: the audit event evaluation.decision_recorded carries the two outcome VALUES (both members of a closed three-value enum, and therefore not tenant content) plus a hash of the rationale. The rationale TEXT itself stays in OBJ-3 behind bypass-free RLS. See NSB-04.

EVALUATE_DECISION_ROLES.semantics: SET INCLUSION over an exhaustively enumerated two-element set.

ROLE_MATRIX.default_designated_decision_role: organization_admin (CS-05). Applied as the column default AND as the explicit value written at T1 when the caller supplies none — never left to a nullable column interpreted as 'the default'.
ROLE_MATRIX.designation_rule: Only organization_admin or impact_manager may be designated as an evaluation's decider (CS-06). Any other value is REFUSED at T1 and is unrepresentable in the column (CLOSED CHECK).

forbidden_decision_roles.note: CS-07. super_admin is forbidden not because it is insufficiently privileged but because platform administration is not tenant decision-making (MO-07). Combined with the six-value role CHECK at db/schema.ts line 113, EVALUATE_DECISION_ROLES and forbidden_decision_roles partition the role space exactly: 2 + 4 = 6, no role unaccounted for.

enforcement_mechanism.required: A closed set-inclusion predicate, declared once in lib/auth/permissions.ts alongside the EXISTING STELLA_ROLES and REVIEW_ROLES precedents, of the shape: const EVALUATE_DECISION_ROLES: readonly Role[] = ['organization_admin', 'impact_manager']; and canDecideEvaluation(role) = EVALUATE_DECISION_ROLES.includes(role).
enforcement_mechanism.FORBIDDEN: hasRole(role, 'organization_admin') and hasRole(role, 'impact_manager') are BOTH forbidden for every Evaluate decision permission (CS-08).
enforcement_mechanism.measured_reason: hasRole is defined as ROLE_HIERARCHY[userRole] >= ROLE_HIERARCHY[requiredRole]. Measured at BASE: super_admin = 100, organization_admin = 80, impact_manager = 60. So hasRole('super_admin','organization_admin') is 100 >= 80 = TRUE and hasRole('super_admin','impact_manager') is 100 >= 60 = TRUE. Either shorthand ADMITS super_admin silently, which CS-07 forbids. The '+' shorthand is not merely imprecise here — it is wrong.
enforcement_mechanism.not_a_new_mechanism: lib/auth/permissions.ts already carries two set-inclusion sets for exactly this reason and says so in its own comments. This package selects the existing pattern rather than introducing one.
enforcement_mechanism.guard_non_collision: lib/auth/__tests__/no-inline-review-role-arrays.test.ts targets only lib/pipeline/sroi-results.ts and lib/pipeline/methodology-review.ts and matches only arrays containing 'reviewer'. A two-element Evaluate set in lib/auth/permissions.ts is outside its TARGET_FILES and contains no 'reviewer'. It does NOT collide.
enforcement_mechanism.runtime_role_source: The acting role must come from the actor's membership in THE EVALUATION'S organization, resolved server-side (current_user_role_in_org(org_id) at the database layer, the session helper at the application layer). It must NEVER come from a client-supplied field, an ambient 'current role' resolved against a different organization, or a platform-level flag.

permission_matrix.note: Creating an evaluation binds a project to a template version; that is a governance act, kept at the same closed set.
Whether analyst may record criterion INPUTS (INPUT != DECISION, so admitting analyst here would not weaken CS-07) was neither ratified in the repository nor supplied by the coordinator.

permission_matrix.mechanism: SET_INCLUSION over EVALUATE_DECISION_ROLES, PLUS equality against the evaluation's designated_decision_role
permission_matrix.note: Both conditions. Set membership alone would let an impact_manager decide an evaluation designated to organization_admin.

permission_matrix.mechanism: Organization membership. Read access is tenancy-scoped, not role-gated beyond membership — matching the treatment of other tenant read models. super_admin is NOT admitted by an Evaluate-specific bypass (NSB-02).

separation_of_duties.reasoning: The repository's SoD precedent (canApproveRunMethodology = isInReviewSet(role) && !isRunAuthor, enforced by assertRunMethodologyApprovalAllowed in lib/pipeline/sroi-results.ts) forbids approving one's OWN run. Whether an Evaluate decider may decide an evaluation they themselves created, or whose criterion responses they recorded, is a product decision that was neither ratified in the repository nor supplied by the coordinator. Imposing it would be guessing; omitting it silently would hide it. Recorded as AG-03.
separation_of_duties.what_is_authorized_now: The decision act must record decided_by and decided_by_role, so that ANY future SoD rule is retroactively checkable against already-decided rows. Recording the actor is authorized; constraining the actor by authorship is not.

TEMPLATE_LIFECYCLE.scope: ORGANIZATION. Every template and every template version belongs to exactly one organization (CS-11). There is no global, seeded, system or cross-organization template, and no template import/copy path is authorized by this package.

states.meaning: A version being composed. NOT selectable by T1.

states.applies_to: OBJ-2 row with published_at NOT NULL
A PUBLISHED OBJ-2 row that a later version names via supersedes_version_id
states.meaning: DERIVED, not stored as a status. Still fully valid for every evaluation that pinned it. NOT selectable for NEW evaluations.

states.applies_to: OBJ-1 row with archived_at NOT NULL
states.meaning: The container is withdrawn: no new version may be created under it and no new evaluation may pin any of its versions. Existing evaluations — including undecided ones — are UNAFFECTED.

TEMPLATE_LIFECYCLE.publication_is_irreversible: There is no unpublish transition. A published version's criteria and DecisionPolicy are the substrate of every recommendation computed from it; retracting it would retroactively unexplain those recommendations. A mistake is corrected by publishing a new version and archiving the container, never by editing or unpublishing.
TEMPLATE_LIFECYCLE.immutability_boundary: OBJ-1 metadata (name, description, archived_at) is mutable. OBJ-2 is append-only in its entirety — criteria_json, decision_policy_json, both hashes, version and ordinal are written once. Renaming a template does NOT change any version identity, which is why definition_hash covers the VERSION payload and not the container's name.
publication_guards: criteria_json contains at least one criterion (ZD-06)
decision_policy_json is TOTAL over the score domain with no gap, no overlap and no fallback branch
definition_hash and decision_policy_hash are computed by the server over a canonical serialization, never supplied by the client
version and ordinal are server-assigned and monotonic per template_id
TEMPLATE_LIFECYCLE.archived_container_does_not_orphan_evalu: Archiving OBJ-1 must NOT cascade to OBJ-2 or OBJ-3. A decided evaluation whose template container was later archived remains fully readable and fully explainable. Stated because a CASCADE here would silently destroy decision provenance.
TEMPLATE_LIFECYCLE.authoring_role: AUTHORITY_GAP — see AG-01. The template lifecycle above is fully specified and implementable; WHO may perform TPL-DRAFT creation and publication is not, and that specific action is NOT_AUTHORIZED until adjudicated.

controls.permitted: Stella MAY analyze an evaluation's inputs, explain a criterion, explain the Score, explain the SYSTEM recommendation, suggest which criteria look weak, and DRAFT rationale text for a human to review (EV-03 permits 'draft rationale' explicitly — PR106's boundary did not enumerate it).

controls.forbidden: Stella MAY NOT score. No Stella output is an input to the scoring function. The scoring function's signature must make this structurally impossible: it accepts (criteria, responses) and nothing else.

Stella MAY NOT produce the authoritative recommendation. The SYSTEM recommendation comes from (Score, DecisionPolicy) only (CS-01). Any Stella-produced outcome-shaped suggestion is ANALYSIS, is labeled as such in the UI, is never written to recommendation_snapshot, and never participates in the divergence computation.

Stella MAY NOT decide or approve. OBJ-3 carries NO Stella-writable column — no stella_recommendation, no stella_score, no stella_outcome, no stella_analysis. Stella's output lives in stella_interactions.response_json, on the other side of the boundary from the decision record. This is a STRUCTURAL control, not a review convention: there is no column for Stella to write.

controls.measured_constraint: At BASE, Stella CANNOT be bound to an evaluation. stella_interactions has project_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES projects.id and NO evaluation_id column, and stella_role is a CLOSED CHECK over exactly six values. Therefore in V1 an Evaluate Stella interaction is recorded against project_id with an OPEN pipeline_step value (pipeline_step is varchar(100) with no CHECK), and it is NOT bound to a specific evaluation. Binding an interaction to an evaluation, or adding an Evaluate-specific stella_role, is DDL and is DEFERRED (DRR-05, DDL_FUTURE).

controls.control: A Stella-drafted rationale is a UI PREFILL only. The persisted decision_rationale is what the designated human submitted at T5, attributed to decided_by. The system must not record a rationale the human did not submit, and must not mark a rationale as human-authored because it passed through a human's screen unedited without submission.

Stella availability is NOT a precondition for any Evaluate transition. Every transition T1..T8 must succeed with Stella unreachable, disabled, unconfigured or erroring. Evaluate degrades to fully functional without AI.
Evaluate must not extend canUseStella. The existing STELLA_ROLES set governs who may invoke Stella; Evaluate consumes it unchanged.

RLS_SECURITY_INVARIANTS.invariant: Every Evaluate relation has ROW LEVEL SECURITY ENABLED and FORCED.
RLS_SECURITY_INVARIANTS.precedent: db/migrations/0068_commercial_account_ce1.sql, which is ENABLE + FORCE with zero policies.

RLS_SECURITY_INVARIANTS.invariant: Every Evaluate relation carries a NOT NULL organization_id, denormalized where necessary, so that no policy needs a join to be correct. The tenant predicate is exactly organization_id = ANY(current_user_org_ids()).
RLS_SECURITY_INVARIANTS.rationale: A policy that joins to reach organization_id is a policy whose correctness depends on the joined row's own policy.

RLS_SECURITY_INVARIANTS.invariant: NO Evaluate policy contains current_user_is_super_admin(). Declared explicitly as an instance of MO-07, because 15 migrations at BASE establish the opposite precedent and a new table written by imitation would inherit it.
RLS_SECURITY_INVARIANTS.verification: A repository-level test asserts zero occurrences of current_user_is_super_admin in the Evaluate migration(s). See the test manifest, N-03 and M-02.

RLS_SECURITY_INVARIANTS.invariant: OBJ-2 has NO UPDATE policy and NO DELETE policy — both denied by omission — plus the uellix_forbid_mutation trigger as defense in depth.

OBJ-3 UPDATE is permitted ONLY while state is pre-DECIDED, and every snapshot column is write-once. A DECIDED row admits no UPDATE at all. DELETE is denied outright on OBJ-3 — a decided evaluation is audit-bearing.

OBJ-4 INSERT and UPDATE are permitted only while the PARENT evaluation is pre-DECIDED. DELETE is permitted only while the parent is pre-DECIDED, and never for an evaluation that has ever been DECIDED.

The DECIDE write path additionally requires the actor's role, resolved via current_user_role_in_org(organization_id), to equal the row's designated_decision_role AND to be a member of the closed two-element set. Membership in the organization is necessary but NOT sufficient for T5.

created_by / recorded_by / decided_by must equal auth.uid() in the WITH CHECK of the writing policy, following the 0045 domain_object_versions_insert precedent (created_by = auth.uid()). A client-supplied actor id is never trusted.

Policies are granted TO uellix_app, not TO public, following the 0045 insert-policy precedent. A future ACL package must GRANT on the Evaluate tables to uellix_app or the runtime cannot read them — recorded because hosted_0007 already enumerates 37 tables and 15 FIB tables lack that grant.

Cross-organization reads are impossible by predicate, not by application filtering. A request whose principal resolves to no organization sees ZERO Evaluate rows — never all rows. Stated because a null/ambient scope has previously resolved to GLOBAL rather than to refusal elsewhere in this repository.
No Evaluate relation is exposed through any anonymous, public or unauthenticated surface (CS-15). There is no public locator, no share token and no verification endpoint for Evaluate in V1.

NO_SUPERADMIN_BYPASS_CONTROLS.control: No Evaluate permission helper may be written with hasRole(). Every Evaluate role predicate is set inclusion over a closed enumerated set.
NO_SUPERADMIN_BYPASS_CONTROLS.why: hasRole('super_admin', X) is true for every X, measured (super_admin = 100 dominates all). This is the exact mechanism by which CS-07 would be violated without anyone writing 'super_admin' anywhere in the diff.

NO_SUPERADMIN_BYPASS_CONTROLS.control: No Evaluate RLS policy grants read or write on the basis of platform-superadmin status (RLS-03).

Evaluate content is NOT stored in any relation whose existing policies already carry the bypass. Concretely: domain_object_versions is REFUSED as the snapshot substrate (DRR-01) even though it is otherwise a perfect structural fit and would require no DDL.
NO_SUPERADMIN_BYPASS_CONTROLS.why: Reusing a bypassed relation imports the bypass. The bypass is a property of where content lives, not of who wrote the feature.

NO_SUPERADMIN_BYPASS_CONTROLS.control: Evaluate audit payloads carry IDENTITY and CLOSED-ENUM VALUES, never verbatim tenant content. before_json and after_json for Evaluate events contain ids, state names, outcome values (members of a closed three-value enum), score_status values, hashes and timestamps — never decision_rationale text, never na_rationale text, never criteria_json.
NO_SUPERADMIN_BYPASS_CONTROLS.why: Measured: audit_logs_select_member_or_admin is USING (organization_id = ANY(current_user_org_ids()) OR current_user_is_super_admin()). Any verbatim rationale placed in after_json becomes readable by every platform superadmin, which reintroduces exactly the standing content bypass CS-12 forbids — through the audit trail rather than through the table.
NO_SUPERADMIN_BYPASS_CONTROLS.reconciliation_with_fail_closed_logger: lib/audit/logger.ts THROWS when entry.contentModifying is true and beforeJson is absent (FIBC-040). That contract is satisfied by supplying a beforeJson of ids, prior state, prior hashes and prior closed-enum values — enough to reconstruct the TRANSITION, which is what FIBC-040 requires — without the content itself. The two requirements are compatible; an implementer must not weaken either to satisfy the other.

NO_SUPERADMIN_BYPASS_CONTROLS.control: There is NO administrative override path: no action, flag, cron, batch job, admin console button, support tool or database function by which a non-designated principal records, alters or reverses a decision; and none by which the SYSTEM recommendation becomes the decision.
NO_SUPERADMIN_BYPASS_CONTROLS.why: CS-07 plus EV-02's 'Human decision remains decisive'. This is an ABSENCE, so the control is a test that proves the absence (see the test manifest, N-06 and M-04) rather than a line of code.

NO_SUPERADMIN_BYPASS_CONTROLS.control: super_admin retains ordinary platform administration — it is not being demoted. What is forbidden is super_admin acting as a TENANT DECIDER or reading tenant Evaluate content by virtue of platform status. Stated so an implementer does not read CS-07 as a general revocation and try to restore access somewhere else.

IMMUTABLE_SNAPSHOTS_AND_VERSIONING.atomicity: All nine are written in the SAME statement as the state transition to DECIDED. A DECIDED row with any snapshot column NULL (other than decision_rationale under DIV-04) must be unrepresentable, not merely unreachable.
IMMUTABLE_SNAPSHOTS_AND_VERSIONING.write_once: No snapshot column may ever be updated after it is written. Enforced by the absence of an UPDATE policy for DECIDED rows (RLS-05) plus the immutability trigger.
IMMUTABLE_SNAPSHOTS_AND_VERSIONING.why_decided_by_role_is_snapshotted: A user's role in an organization can change after a decision. Snapshotting the role AT DECISION TIME is what keeps 'a designated role decided this' verifiable years later, and is what makes any future SoD or role-audit rule retroactively checkable.
IMMUTABLE_SNAPSHOTS_AND_VERSIONING.why_score_is_snapshotted_and_also_deriva: The Score remains derivable from OBJ-4 and the pinned OBJ-2, and it is ALSO snapshotted. That redundancy is deliberate and is a CONTROL: a mismatch between the snapshot and a fresh recomputation over unchanged inputs proves that something which was supposed to be immutable changed. See the test manifest, M-05.
IMMUTABLE_SNAPSHOTS_AND_VERSIONING.no_second_lineage: Evaluate introduces exactly ONE version lineage — OBJ-2's, keyed by (template_id, version) with a monotonic ordinal and supersedes_version_id. DecisionPolicy does not have its own. Evaluations do not have their own.

AUDIT.vocabulary_reuse_finding: Existing vocabulary CANNOT express Evaluate events, because no Evaluate OBJECT exists in it: AUDIT_ACTIONS has 111 keys at BASE and zero matching 'evaluation'. What IS reusable is the VERB morphology, and it is reused rather than reinvented — .created, .updated, .archived, .upserted, .recorded plus the object-specific submitted_for_decision and decision_recorded, all following the established <object>.<verb> shape.

new_keys.note: A refused decision — wrong role, wrong designated role, or SCORE_NOT_COMPUTABLE — is AUDITED, not silently dropped. A refusal that leaves no trace is indistinguishable from an attempt that never happened.

new_keys.verb_precedent: object-specific publication verb, following canPublishReportDisclosure's vocabulary shape

AUDIT.payload_contract: See NSB-04. Identity, closed-enum values, hashes and timestamps only. NEVER decision_rationale text, na_rationale text or criteria_json.
AUDIT.fail_closed_reuse: Evaluate uses logAuditAction unchanged. It must NOT be wrapped in a try/catch that swallows AuditContractViolationError, and an Evaluate transition must NOT be committed when its audit write fails — the whole point of the fail-closed logger (FIBC-040) is that a governed transition does not appear successful when its audit contract was not satisfied.
AUDIT.atomicity: The audit write and the state transition must be in the SAME database transaction. An audited-but-not-applied transition and an applied-but-not-audited transition are both defects.

read_model_boundary.authorized: Authenticated, organization-scoped pages and server actions under app/app/**.
forbidden_in_v1: Any Evaluate report artifact, PDF or export
Any verification hash or content-integrity locator for Evaluate
Any external webhook, API key surface or machine-to-machine endpoint
read_model_boundary.anchor: RI-01 forbids resurrecting obsolete report/hash/RPC designs; Report Integrity requires its own future authority. Evaluate V1 therefore produces no report artifact at all.

route_location.closed_world: Exactly these two candidates. Any third location — under trust-center, under organization, under portfolios, or a top-level route outside app/app — is FORBIDDEN by this package without a further amendment.
route_location.why_not_decided_here: Neither the repository nor the coordinator adjudicated it. RE_U3 records EVALUATE as a FIRST_CLASS_TARGET_NODE with route null, which establishes that Evaluate IS a primary product area in the target IA but deliberately does NOT assign it a route ('IA reservation only... No placeholder route'). Choosing between the two candidates is a product/IA decision, and guessing it would put a route in the wrong place in a first-class area.

nav_constraints.rule: NAV_LINKS must NOT gain an Evaluate entry until a real runtime route exists.
nav_constraints.anchor: RE_U3: EVALUATE_NAV_STATUS = NAV_RESERVED_FOR_FUTURE_RUNTIME, and dead_placeholder_links = 'NONE added; EVALUATE and MEASURE intentionally have no top-level nav entry rather than a disabled/placeholder one'.
nav_constraints.measured: NAV_LINKS has 7 entries at BASE, none Evaluate.

nav_constraints.rule: When the route lands, the nav entry is added to components/layout/nav-links.ts ONLY — never to Sidebar.tsx or MobileNav.tsx directly.
nav_constraints.why: That file is the single source of truth precisely because desktop and mobile previously each carried their own copy and silently diverged (RE-U1 U1-F10).

nav_constraints.rule: No Evaluate route may assume /app resolves. Measured at BASE: app/app/ has layout.tsx and loading.tsx but NO page.tsx, so a redirect or link to /app terminates in a 404. Evaluate must link to a concrete leaf route.

enforcement_topology.rule: A layout does NOT wrap a route handler. Every Evaluate route handler under app/**/route.ts must carry its own principal and organization resolution; a page-level or layout-level gate does not protect a sibling handler.
enforcement_topology.why_stated: This is a measured repository-wide failure mode. Evaluate is authorized to add server actions and, if needed, route handlers; both must gate independently.
enforcement_topology.authoritative_layer: SERVER. Every permission and every transition guard is enforced server-side. A disabled button, a hidden menu item or a client-side role check is never an enforcement layer.

broad_evaluate.rule: Broad Evaluate — creating a template version, recording criterion inputs, computing the Score and the SYSTEM recommendation, and recording a human decision — requires NO approved SROI run (CS-18) and NO stella_findings substrate (CS-17).
broad_evaluate.why_defensible: Measured object ownership: stella_findings is FIBDB-019 and stella_finding_dispositions is FIBDB-020, both owned by FIBIU-20 at topological_level 3.2; FIBDB-040 (sroi_run_reviews.sod_trigger) is also FIBIU-20's. Evaluate has no object that FKs to any FIBIU-19 or FIBIU-20 object under the model above. Gating broad Evaluate on FIBIU-20 would be Evaluate annexing another unit's dependency, not honoring one.
broad_evaluate.wave3_note: RE_U3 records EVALUATE_RUNTIME_STATUS = WAIT_FOR_WAVE3_CONTRACT and RE_U4 ties Evaluate hosting to Wave 4 (FIBIU-21/22). This package does NOT unilaterally lift either. It reduces the question to a precise one for the HPO: the Wave-3 wait was recorded when no Evaluate object model existed; under the model above, broad Evaluate has no FIBIU-19/20 object dependency, so what remains of the wait is an AUTHORITY question and not a data one. Recorded as AG-05, NOT resolved here. This package authorizes no implementation that lifts it.

narrow_run_review.rule: The NARROW FIB run-review dependency is PRESERVED exactly where FIB governs it (CS-19). Evaluate does NOT absorb, replace, relocate, rename or re-implement it.
narrow_run_review.what_is_preserved: lib/pipeline/methodology-review.ts, lib/pipeline/sroi-results.ts (assertRunMethodologyApprovalAllowed at line 317, called at 451 and 507), sroi_run_reviews, the review set via isInReviewSet, canApproveRunMethodology(role, isRunAuthor), and FIBDB-040's future sod_trigger — all remain owned by FIB / FIBIU-20.
narrow_run_review.relationship: RE_U3 calls methodology-review a CURRENT_IMPLEMENTATION_SUBSET of the future Evaluate area. That is an IA statement about product surface, NOT a licence to migrate the code. RE_U3's own prohibition_observed says it 'did not rename or relocate lib/pipeline/methodology-review.ts'. This package observes the same prohibition.
narrow_run_review.consequence_for_implementers: Where an Evaluate criterion needs to reflect a run's methodology-review status, it READS that status. It does not re-decide it, does not write to sroi_run_reviews, and does not reuse Evaluate's decision path to approve a run.

what_is_explicitly_NOT_done: No entitlement check anywhere in Evaluate
No entitlement_grants row, index or migration
No capability catalogue is created, extended or relocated
No Evaluate transition is gated on any entitlement
No quota, metering or usage counter for Evaluate
ENTITLEMENT_RESERVATION.why_reservation_only: Measured: COMMERCIAL_ACCOUNT_ENTITLEMENT_AUTHORITY_v1.0.0.json places capability_key in entitlement_grants as 'product-capability identity, from a closed catalogue owned by the implementing node', with exactly one live grant per (organization_id, capability_key) enforced by a partial unique index WHERE effective_to IS NULL. That catalogue is CE-3's, not Evaluate's. Evaluate creating or extending it would be a shared-writer collision with an unlanded node.
ENTITLEMENT_RESERVATION.obligation_on_ce3: CE-3's implementing node should honor 'evaluate.v1' as a reserved member of its closed catalogue. This package records the claim; it does not amend CE-3's authority and cannot.
ENTITLEMENT_RESERVATION.v1_availability: In Commercial V1, Evaluate is available to every organization that can reach it, gated by ROLE and TENANCY only. Adding entitlement gating later is additive and requires its own authority.

IMPLEMENTATION_SURFACE.note: Write-surface CLASSES with exact path patterns and ordering constraints. This package AUTHORIZES NO IMPLEMENTATION — every class below requires its own governed node with its own ODS allocation, its own test manifest and its own grant where a protected surface is touched.

classes.name: DB / DDL
classes.protected: db/migrations/** IS in DEFAULT_PROTECTED_PATTERNS and REQUIRES a protected grant. db/schema.ts is NOT protected.
classes.ordering: MUST be first. Every other class depends on it.
classes.ordinal: NOT ALLOCATED HERE. NO migration ordinal is assigned by this package. The ordinal is re-derived at the implementing node's own sync point against the then-current ceiling (0069 at BASE).
classes.generation_constraint: The migration must be produced by a normal drizzle-kit generate over an edited db/schema.ts, with any non-generatable governance DDL added as a bounded patch — never authored as a --custom stub, whose provenance cannot be re-proven.

classes.name: Pure scoring and DecisionPolicy engine
classes.ordering: Parallelizable with W-EV-1 — it depends on the TYPES, not on the tables.
constraints: Pure functions only: no db import, no fetch, no Date.now, no Math.random, no process.env
The scoring function's signature accepts (criteria, responses) and NOTHING else, so SB-02 is structural
Returns a discriminated result carrying score_status — never a bare number plus a nullable error

classes.name: Permissions
constraints: Adds EVALUATE_DECISION_ROLES as a closed readonly two-element set beside the existing STELLA_ROLES and REVIEW_ROLES
Adds canDecideEvaluation, canCreateEvaluation, canArchiveEvaluation as set-inclusion predicates
MUST NOT use hasRole for any Evaluate predicate (NSB-01)
MUST NOT modify hasRole, ROLE_HIERARCHY, STELLA_ROLES, REVIEW_ROLES, isInReviewSet or canApproveRunMethodology

classes.name: Audit vocabulary
constraints: Adds exactly the 10 keys in AUDIT.new_keys, taking AUDIT_ACTIONS from 111 to 121
MUST NOT alter logAuditAction's fail-closed validation
MUST NOT add a contentModifying exemption for Evaluate

classes.name: Server actions
constraints: Every action resolves the principal and the organization server-side and independently
Every transition guard from TRANSITION_MATRIX is enforced here
Refusals are audited (evaluation.decision_refused), never silent

classes.name: UI read model
classes.ordering: After W-EV-5. BLOCKED on AG-04 (route location) — exactly one of the two path patterns above is authorized once AG-04 is adjudicated, never both.
constraints: In-app, authenticated, organization-scoped only (CS-15)
Displays Score, score_status, SYSTEM recommendation, decision and divergence as DISTINCT labeled things (RE_U3: INPUT != SCORE != RECOMMENDATION != DECISION)
Stella analysis is visually labeled as analysis and never adjacent-styled to the SYSTEM recommendation
No nav entry until the route exists (NAV-01)

classes.name: Stella advisory boundary
constraints: READ-only with respect to every Evaluate relation
Writes only to stella_interactions, bound to project_id with an open pipeline_step value (SB-05)
MUST NOT add a stella_role value (that is DDL on a closed CHECK — DRR-05)
Evaluate must function fully with Stella unavailable (SB-07)

classes.name: Tests
constraints: Every control in the companion test manifest is realized
RLS invariants are proven against a REAL PostgreSQL instance via the disposable harness, never asserted from SQL text alone

AUTHORITY_GAPS.gap: Which role may author and publish an evaluation template version.
AUTHORITY_GAPS.fail_closed_position: NO role may author or publish a template until adjudicated. canAuthorEvaluationTemplate is NOT_AUTHORIZED_UNTIL_ADJUDICATED and W-EV-6's template-authoring surface is blocked.
AUTHORITY_GAPS.what_IS_authorized: The full template lifecycle — states, immutability, publication guards, hashes, non-cascade — is specified and implementable. Only the AUTHORING ACTOR is blocked.
AUTHORITY_GAPS.candidates_for_the_HPO_to_consider: organization_admin only (narrowest, consistent with CS-05's default decider), or the closed EVALUATE_DECISION_ROLES set. Listed as candidates, NOT as a recommendation this package is entitled to make.

AUTHORITY_GAPS.gap: Which role may record criterion INPUTS (canRecordEvaluationInput).
AUTHORITY_GAPS.note: INPUT != DECISION is ratified (RE_U3), so admitting analyst here would NOT violate CS-07 — CS-07 constrains the DECISION role. But 'would not violate' is not 'is ratified'. The existing repository precedent for input-level work is canUploadEvidence at analyst level; the precedent for assessment work is isInReviewSet, which includes reviewer. Both are plausible and they disagree, which is exactly why this is a gap and not an inference.

AUTHORITY_GAPS.gap: Whether an Evaluate decider may decide an evaluation they created or whose inputs they recorded (separation of duties).
AUTHORITY_GAPS.fail_closed_position: NOT_IMPOSED and NOT_WAIVED. No SoD constraint is authorized, and none is forbidden.
AUTHORITY_GAPS.mitigation_authorized_now: decided_by and decided_by_role are snapshotted, so any future SoD rule is retroactively checkable against rows already decided.

AUTHORITY_GAPS.gap: Evaluate route location: primary area versus project sub-area.
AUTHORITY_GAPS.status: NOT_RATIFIED — RE_U3 assigns route null deliberately
AUTHORITY_GAPS.fail_closed_position: No route is invented. W-EV-6 is BLOCKED on this. The candidate set is CLOSED to exactly two (ROUTING.route_location).

AUTHORITY_GAPS.gap: Whether RE_U3's EVALUATE_RUNTIME_STATUS = WAIT_FOR_WAVE3_CONTRACT still gates broad Evaluate, given that broad Evaluate under this object model has no FIBIU-19/20 object dependency.
AUTHORITY_GAPS.status: OPEN. This package does NOT lift it.
AUTHORITY_GAPS.fail_closed_position: The wait stands until amended. This package narrows the question to an authority question and authorizes no implementation that would lift it.

RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.risk: An implementer writes canDecideEvaluation with hasRole(role,'impact_manager') because it reads as 'impact_manager and above' and is the dominant idiom in lib/auth/permissions.ts (7 of its helpers use that shape).
RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.impact: super_admin silently becomes a tenant decider. CS-07 and CS-12 both violated, with no occurrence of the string 'super_admin' anywhere in the diff to notice.
RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.control: NSB-01, plus test-manifest N-01 and M-01.

RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.risk: An implementer stores decision_rationale verbatim in audit after_json, because 40+ existing audit verbs carry verbatim content.
RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.impact: Tenant decision content becomes readable by every platform superadmin through audit_logs_select_member_or_admin. CS-12 violated via the audit trail.

RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.risk: An implementer reuses domain_object_versions for template versions because it fits structurally and needs no DDL.
RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.impact: Template criteria and DecisionPolicy land behind the super_admin read bypass.

RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.risk: An implementer represents SCORE_NOT_COMPUTABLE as 0, -1, null or NaN.
RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.impact: A sentinel number is comparable against DecisionPolicy bands, so an all-N/A evaluation silently acquires a recommendation and becomes decidable. CS-03 defeated.
RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.control: ZD-03, ZD-04, plus test-manifest N-02 and M-03.

RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.risk: An implementer stores a divergence boolean 'for query performance'.
RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.impact: A third value that can disagree with the two snapshots it summarizes.

RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.risk: An implementer recomputes the recommendation at read time instead of reading recommendation_snapshot when rendering a decided evaluation.
RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.impact: A historical divergence finding can change after the fact.

RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.risk: An implementer treats an UNANSWERED criterion as a governed N/A.
RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.impact: An empty evaluation reaches READY_FOR_DECISION with a vacuous SCORE_NOT_COMPUTABLE, and CS-03's block becomes indistinguishable from ordinary incompleteness.

RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.risk: An implementer migrates lib/pipeline/methodology-review.ts into Evaluate because RE_U3 calls it a CURRENT_IMPLEMENTATION_SUBSET of Evaluate.
RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.impact: CS-19 violated; a FIB-governed, FIBIU-20-owned surface is annexed and its SoD precedent is disturbed.

RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.risk: A future ACL package omits GRANT on the Evaluate tables to uellix_app.
RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.impact: RLS is correct but the runtime reads nothing. Measured precedent: hosted_0007 enumerates 37 tables and 15 FIB tables lack the grant.
RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.control: RLS-09; carried forward to the ACL successor, not solvable here.

RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.risk: This package is read as lifting the Wave-3 wait.
RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.impact: Implementation proceeds without the authority amendment AG-05 requires.
RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.control: AG-05 states explicitly that the wait stands and that no implementation lifting it is authorized.
